scope.description: Top-level index of every family under build/rk3588-example-captures with a manifest.
scope.board_access: none; no ssh/scp, no submit, no FPGA program/flash
scope.capture_rule: A case is never marked captured until a results directory contains a real output BO. A CPU oracle is never stored as output.

status_definitions.prepared: READY, official runner validation OK, no results directory with real output BOs.
status_definitions.running_on_board: Exclusive board worker has submitted the case; capture in progress.
status_definitions.captured_unverified: Results directory contains real output BOs but no completed oracle comparison.
status_definitions.verified: Results directory contains real output BOs, submit_ret==0 for every case, and oracle comparison PASS.
status_definitions.verified_runner_invalid: Verified by real capture and oracle comparison, but the current runner rejects the bundle for a rerun (odd-word fetch extent). Not counted as blocked.
status_definitions.blocked: Manifest BLOCKED or official runner validation FAIL; must not be submitted.
status_definitions.blocked_runner_invalid: Manifest READY but the current official runner validation rejects the bundle; must not be submitted until regenerated/revalidated.

current_board.note: This index was built on the host and did not query the board. No in-flight capture is visible from host-side evidence. The last known board worker was the ew-int capture, which completed at 2026-11-05T20:04:25Z and whose results were copied back. If a worker is running now, it owns the exclusive lock and this queue must not start until it releases it.
pre_start_gate: Do not start while any capture/rocket process is present; the current worker owns the board.
Acquire flock -x -w 900 /home/opencode-agent/rk3588-npu.lock around the whole runner invocation.
Record hostname, kernel, python version, /dev/accel/accel0 and a pgrep snapshot before the first submit.
Use a fresh run/output root; never overwrite an existing capture.json or output BO.
Copy results back and rehash before starting the next family.

deferred_families.reason: All 7 READY cases fail the current official runner validation because the task declares 51 or 69 regcmd words while regcmd.bin contains exactly 51 or 69 QWORDs. The family validator passes, but it does not model the current runner's fetch extent.

The source proves DIV/FLOOR/CEIL use floating-point semantics and are not integer operations (OPERATIONS[...]['integer_supported'] = False). There is no trustworthy integer oracle; bundling them as integer EW would mislabel the result. FLOOR and CEIL share this blocker.

The only multi-input sum in either source is FP16, with FP32 BRDMA/NRDMA operands. This family is integer-only (ew-int); an FP16/FP32 mixed case needs its own oracle and belongs in an ew-fp16 family. It is not an INT8/INT16/INT32 case and was deliberately not materialized here.
ReLU-X and PReLU are emitted only in the FP16 BS/BN auxiliary stages. No integer ReLU path exists in either source, and ReLU6 and batchnorm are never emitted at all. Not an integer elementwise case.
